assertions: The original two-file regression failed 9 of 87 tests because rejected, malformed, or uncertain email outcomes could still be stamped and an expired voucher could still be submitted.
The final six-file focused suite passed 115 of 115 tests.
Provider rejection, non-2xx, malformed success, timeout, invalid provider-ID type, and post-acceptance stamp failure no longer become false success; retries use the same server-derived key.
The first accepted provider payload is persisted and reused across tenant-branding drift or a later branding lookup failure; a first-attempt branding failure does not submit a provider request.
Voucher age is rechecked immediately before each sequential send and by the claim RPC, so a row crossing the 24-hour boundary is not newly submitted.

After source and tenant identity validation, a delayed overlapping worker can replay a recorded acceptance after another worker stamps the source without another provider submission, duplicate accepted count, or false failure; unaccepted work still requires current eligibility.

The disposable PostgreSQL suite applied the additive intent migration and passed 164 of 164 checks, including service-only permissions, source-derived authority, payload freezing, and accepted-intent replay.
Edge checks, TypeScript, targeted ESLint with 13 pre-existing warnings and no errors, diff checks, and the production build with synthetic public configuration passed.
The full unit suite passed 1176 tests, failed the same 3 pinned-companion UI-contract assertions as baseline, and skipped 1.
failed_assertions: Three pre-existing mobile-first companion-source contract assertions remain failed and block a fully green release suite.
skips: One existing unit test is skipped.
limitations: No genuine email provider, delivery receipt, shared database, staging, production, browser E2E, load, soak, deployment, or canary operation was exercised.
Provider behavior was simulated; provider acceptance is not delivery.
The additive migration is locally exercised only and its actual target migration ledger must be verified before deployment, especially relative to the locked 20260920090000 pricing migration.
The hold-expiry sibling now reports provider acceptance or failure and uses a durable intent, but rediscovery after expiry, claim/lease fairness, and backlog recovery remain open under COR-04.
The independent reviewer's requested model and effort were supplied by the host, but effective runtime metadata was not independently observable.

artifacts.notes: 1176 pass, 3 unchanged companion UI-contract failures, 1 skip.

independent_review.limitations: Approval covers COR-02A only, including the narrow COR-04 sibling hardening; it is not deployment or release approval.
